instruction.name: movgr2fr.d
instruction.description: Move the 64 bits of rj into fd.

latencies.notes: 2 cycles for this direction. The split between the two directions is not observable on this core: every closed chain crosses the boundary both ways, so only the sum shows up (the round trip measures 4.00 cycles and stays additive). The split is fixed by the microarchitecture: an FPR load cannot take the address-bypass path, so `fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0` (6.98 cycles) has to be a 5-cycle load plus a 2-cycle move, and the 4.00-cycle FPR round trip then puts the other direction at 2. The stored experiment is the round trip itself, with the opposite direction subtracted as chain_latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f1, $r5; movgr2fr.d $f2, $r6; movgr2fr.d $f3, $r7; movgr2fr.d $f4, $r8; movgr2fr.d $f5, $r9; movgr2fr.d $f6, $r10; movgr2fr.d $f7, $r11
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --init 'li.d $r4, 1; li.d $r5, 2; li.d $r6, 3; li.d $r7, 4; li.d $r8, 5; li.d $r9, 6; li.d $r10, 7; li.d $r11, 8' --asm 'movgr2fr.d $f0, $r4; movgr2fr.d $f1, $r5; movgr2fr.d $f2, $r6; movgr2fr.d $f3, $r7; movgr2fr.d $f4, $r8; movgr2fr.d $f5, $r9; movgr2fr.d $f6, $r10; movgr2fr.d $f7, $r11'

notes: Individual GPR->FPR latency is 1 cycle. Round trip with movfr2gr.d is 4 cycles; high-half round trip movgr2frh.w + movfrh2gr.s is 5 cycles. 3+2 cycles for movgr2fr/movfr2gr is incompatible with the 4-cycle full round trip. Throughput is 1 CPI for 1-20 independent lanes.
